{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "For Java SDK (U1): Use gRPC and protobuf to communicate with Fabric peers and orderers, following the existing Node.js SDK architecture.",
    "For Python SDK (U2): Use gRPC and protobuf, leveraging existing Python gRPC libraries; implement similar client structure as Java SDK.",
    "For pre-built chaincode deployment (U3): Support Docker images for common architectures (amd64, arm64); modify peer to accept a pre-built image reference instead of requiring source code.",
    "For VSCC logging improvement (U4): Add INFO-level logging that displays the policy, signer names and orgs, and lacking signers; propagate failure details to the event notification system for SDK consumption.",
    "For platform-specific binaries (U5): Set up a CI pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions) to build binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows for all Fabric tools (configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, etc.).",
    "For certificate pinning (U6): Implement the simpler endpoint-based fingerprint list mechanism (check at endorsement time) using an Auth Handler, as recommended in the spec.",
    "For quick start test network (U7): Provide a script (e.g., using Docker Compose) and update the testing documentation with step-by-step instructions and links to existing test tools.",
    "For default configuration consolidation (U8): Create a 'config_defaults' directory containing core.yaml, orderer.yaml, and configtx.yaml with all default values extracted from source code; update documentation and BYFN instructions."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing Hyperledger Fabric source code is available and the developer has full write access to the repository.",
    "No Java or Python SDK implementations exist in the current codebase; they are to be built from scratch.",
    "The developer has moderate familiarity with Fabric internals and the Go programming language for peer modifications.",
    "All code changes will be accompanied by unit tests and integration tests using the existing Fabric test framework.",
    "Documentation updates will be contributed to the official Hyperledger Fabric documentation (readthedocs).",
    "Effort estimates are based on a single developer working full-time on this increment, excluding project management overhead.",
    "The pre-built chaincode deployment only needs to support Docker container packaging; other packaging formats are out of scope.",
    "The certificate pinning feature only implements the endpoint-based fingerprint list; the channel-based list is deferred.",
    "The quick start test network will be a minimal single-node network for development and testing purposes.",
    "Default configuration consolidation covers all components mentioned in U8 (peer, gossip, ledger, endorser, orderer, Kafka, configtx).",
    "All estimates are in work-hours and represent the most likely effort for each activity."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Java SDK Implementation (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a Java SDK to interact with Hyperledger Fabric, including gRPC client, protobuf message handling, chaincode invocation, event listening, and comprehensive unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 200
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Python SDK Implementation (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a Python SDK to interact with Hyperledger Fabric, covering gRPC client, protobuf support, chaincode operations, event handling, and tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 150
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Pre-built Chaincode Deployment (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Modify the Fabric peer to accept and deploy user chaincode in pre-built Docker image form, update chaincode lifecycle and packaging logic, and provide tooling to generate pre-built images for multiple architectures.",
      "most_likely_effort": 120
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Improved VSCC Validation Logging (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Enhance the VSCC (Validation System Chaincode) to log detailed policy information, signer names/orgs, and missing signatures at INFO level when validation fails, and propagate failure details to the event notification system.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Platform-Specific Binary Downloads (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Set up CI/CD pipeline to build and release platform-specific binaries (Linux, macOS, Windows) for all Fabric tools (configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, etc.) and provide download instructions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 60
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Certificate Pinning via Fingerprint List (U6)",
      "activity_description": "Implement certificate fingerprint pinning by allowing endorsers to fetch a fingerprint list from a registered domain at endorsement time, using an Auth Handler, and integrate with channel configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 100
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Quick Start Test Network (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Create a simple script (e.g., Docker Compose based) to quickly spin up a minimal Fabric network, update testing documentation with usage instructions and links to existing test tools.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Default Configuration Consolidation (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Audit all component source code to extract default configuration values, update core.yaml, orderer.yaml, and configtx.yaml with complete defaults, place them in a 'config_defaults' directory, and update documentation and BYFN instructions.",
      "most_likely_effort": 50
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "System Integration and Final Documentation",
      "activity_description": "Perform cross-story integration testing, resolve conflicts, ensure consistent behavior across all features, and finalize documentation updates for the entire increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 880
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: For Java SDK (U1): Use gRPC and protobuf to communicate with Fabric peers and orderers, following the existing Node.js SDK architecture.
For Python SDK (U2): Use gRPC and protobuf, leveraging existing Python gRPC libraries; implement similar client structure as Java SDK.
For pre-built chaincode deployment (U3): Support Docker images for common architectures (amd64, arm64); modify peer to accept a pre-built image reference instead of requiring source code.

For VSCC logging improvement (U4): Add INFO-level logging that displays the policy, signer names and orgs, and lacking signers; propagate failure details to the event notification system for SDK consumption.

For platform-specific binaries (U5): Set up a CI pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions) to build binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows for all Fabric tools (configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, etc.).
For certificate pinning (U6): Implement the simpler endpoint-based fingerprint list mechanism (check at endorsement time) using an Auth Handler, as recommended in the spec.
For quick start test network (U7): Provide a script (e.g., using Docker Compose) and update the testing documentation with step-by-step instructions and links to existing test tools.

For default configuration consolidation (U8): Create a 'config_defaults' directory containing core.yaml, orderer.yaml, and configtx.yaml with all default values extracted from source code; update documentation and BYFN instructions.
assumptions: The existing Hyperledger Fabric source code is available and the developer has full write access to the repository.
No Java or Python SDK implementations exist in the current codebase; they are to be built from scratch.
The developer has moderate familiarity with Fabric internals and the Go programming language for peer modifications.
All code changes will be accompanied by unit tests and integration tests using the existing Fabric test framework.
Documentation updates will be contributed to the official Hyperledger Fabric documentation (readthedocs).
Effort estimates are based on a single developer working full-time on this increment, excluding project management overhead.
The pre-built chaincode deployment only needs to support Docker container packaging; other packaging formats are out of scope.
The certificate pinning feature only implements the endpoint-based fingerprint list; the channel-based list is deferred.
The quick start test network will be a minimal single-node network for development and testing purposes.
Default configuration consolidation covers all components mentioned in U8 (peer, gossip, ledger, endorser, orderer, Kafka, configtx).
All estimates are in work-hours and represent the most likely effort for each activity.

activities.activity_description: Design and implement a Java SDK to interact with Hyperledger Fabric, including gRPC client, protobuf message handling, chaincode invocation, event listening, and comprehensive unit and integration tests.
Design and implement a Python SDK to interact with Hyperledger Fabric, covering gRPC client, protobuf support, chaincode operations, event handling, and tests.

Modify the Fabric peer to accept and deploy user chaincode in pre-built Docker image form, update chaincode lifecycle and packaging logic, and provide tooling to generate pre-built images for multiple architectures.

Enhance the VSCC (Validation System Chaincode) to log detailed policy information, signer names/orgs, and missing signatures at INFO level when validation fails, and propagate failure details to the event notification system.

Set up CI/CD pipeline to build and release platform-specific binaries (Linux, macOS, Windows) for all Fabric tools (configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, etc.) and provide download instructions.

Implement certificate fingerprint pinning by allowing endorsers to fetch a fingerprint list from a registered domain at endorsement time, using an Auth Handler, and integrate with channel configuration.
Create a simple script (e.g., Docker Compose based) to quickly spin up a minimal Fabric network, update testing documentation with usage instructions and links to existing test tools.

Audit all component source code to extract default configuration values, update core.yaml, orderer.yaml, and configtx.yaml with complete defaults, place them in a 'config_defaults' directory, and update documentation and BYFN instructions.
Perform cross-story integration testing, resolve conflicts, ensure consistent behavior across all features, and finalize documentation updates for the entire increment.
